analysis.session_summary: The window was led by commodity/FX outperformance: AUD +0.262% and CAD +0.241%, while JPY was weakest at -0.314%. DXY slipped only -0.065% and VIX rose 4.335%, but there was no headline catalyst behind the G10 tape; leg notes repeatedly flag flow/technical. BOE Governor Bailey's appearance was a non-event: GBP basket moved 0.000%. EUR/USD closed +3.1 pips after three uncaused legs.

themes.evidence: All major legs flagged no clear catalyst; EUR/USD legs were +42.7, -84.3, +49.0 pips.
BOE Gov Bailey Speaks produced a basket move of 0.000%, inside the noise floor.

currency_drivers.USD: No clear catalyst in window; soft despite small DXY slip.
currency_drivers.JPY: No clear catalyst; weakest of majors.
currency_drivers.GBP: BOE Bailey was muted, no net impulse.
currency_drivers.AUD: No clear catalyst; strongest of majors.
currency_drivers.CAD: No clear catalyst; selling rejected and recovered.
currency_drivers.CHF: No clear catalyst; held its range.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped +42.7, -84.3 and +49.0 pips across three legs, closing only +3.1 pips with no leg catalyst.

scenarios.name: Commodity FX extension
scenarios.thesis: AUD and CAD ended strongest with no catalyst, so carry/flow bid extends in quiet tape.
triggers: Canada CPI in line or soft

pair_paths.rationale: AUD was strongest and closed at its best; last up leg was +36.7 pips.
JPY weakest; last USD/JPY up leg was +33.7 pips.

scenarios.thesis: Uncaused legs mean moves are likely to fade; choppy ranges persist with no macro driver.
triggers: EUR/USD returns toward full range 88.5 pips
USD/CAD bounces from close near low
scenarios.invalidation: Fresh macro catalyst breaks the range.

pair_paths.rationale: Three legs had no catalyst and pair closed +3.1 pips, within an 88.5-pip range.
USD/CAD closed near low and last up leg was +24.1 pips.

scenarios.name: USD recovery / risk wobble
scenarios.thesis: VIX rose 4.335% while DXY slipped only -0.065%; a further vol spike can lift USD broadly.

pair_paths.rationale: USD/CHF last up leg was +33.2 pips and can recover if USD firms.

risks.why_it_matters: CAD is second-strongest after no catalyst, so a hot CPI could extend CAD strength or unwind if soft.
VIX rose 4.335% while DXY barely moved; a vol spike could force USD short covering.
JPY is weakest and multiple Ueda headlines appeared; any hawkish shift can squeeze shorts.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: High-impact Canada CPI at 14:30: CPI m/m forecast 0.2% vs -0.1% prior, median and trimmed seen 2.0% and 1.9%; can alter CAD strength and risk tone.
